rows.what the ink shows: The first glyph has a long left downstroke turning upward into a right shoulder, then a short terminal descent; this is the visible μ form above the lowered AA*.
After the equals sign, the glyph again has a long descending left stem and an ascending right shoulder ending in a short downstroke, supporting μ.
Beneath the crossing strokes, the initial capital P has its large upper bowl; the following low rounded strokes include a second descending p and a compressed dotted ending before the underline.
The isolated letter after “si” has a long top cross-stroke and one descending stem curling right at its foot; there is no separately visible middle bar.
The overwritten marginal numeral retains a curved upper entrance, a descending diagonal and a broad rightward bottom foot, the distinguishable structure of 2.

After the clear baseline BA, one heavily cancelled baseline glyph retains a lower opening. Small upper-right prongs are visible, but neither the original baseline bowls nor a separate raised star can be isolated securely from the cancellation.

The single baseline letter after BA retains a left stem and upper, middle and lower rightward strokes, but the thick curved cancellation closes their right side; the apparent counters therefore cannot distinguish B from an originally open E. The nearby upper-right stroke merges into the curved crossing at the parenthesis, so a separate raised star is also unsecured.
Under the inserted angular A, the earlier letter retains a rounded upper lobe to the left and a rounded lower lobe to the right, joined by its descending stem: B.
The underlined word begins with a small curved s and low connector, then two conspicuous descending p strokes; the remaining compressed rounded sequence finishes with a hooked s.
The word has a tall descending p, a short r shoulder, then small rounded and flattened cursive strokes; the final stroke carries a distinct high acute accent, supporting prouvé.
Inside 1+…, the dark baseline B shows a left upright and two rounded right bowls. One separate short oblique prime stands above its upper right, before the closing parenthesis.
Between the parentheses is one narrow rounded B, with a small upper turn and a longer lower lobe. There is no angular crossbar or separate raised prime as required for A′.

A heavily retraced upright before the opening parenthesis has an upper return, a middle arm and a lower hooked end. Overlapping closed-looking compartments prevent securely separating E from a B-like underform.
The sequence has the small looped d and low ans, a separate tall l with low a, then a tall d and long compressed deuxième with its raised accent and dotted i.
After la, a long heavy horizontal cancellation covers the word bodies. A small central hump and a short raised remnant remain, but no recoverable letter sequence distinguishes a word.
The inserted word above the deletion starts with a tall hooked t/r gesture, followed by a low rounded join and a detached trailing ce stroke. Its compact joined shape supports trace.
The f has a tall descending entry and rising return; two dots sit over the following compressed low strokes, with a short final e before the comma.
A rounded initial a joins a tall looped l, followed by a low o/r sequence and a right-hooking final s before the closing parenthesis.
Between 1 and A there is one short horizontal stroke with a thickened right tip and no vertical crossing. The nearby plus in the right-hand subscript has a distinct crossing upright.

The open O and joined n, low est, ramené opening r/a and raised final accent, detached à, and the long p descender of prouver survive the sloping deletion. Several interior joins lie under the cancellation.

Two baseline glyphs are visible: a retraced triangular Delta and a separate B with an upright and two right bowls. The lower overlapping strokes stay within these glyphs; no distinct raised or lowered index is visible.
The sign has a thick, roughly rectangular upper horizontal bar and a separate lower parallel bar. The left edge is overfilled but does not preserve a distinct open angle.

Tr has a high sweeping T cap and a small following r. The last baseline capital has a pointed sloping outline and projecting cross-stroke suggestive of A, but dense retracing also conceals possible E arms.
The small marginal deletion above Nous is crossed by a long heavy line; only a short downward hook, a dot and a thick low tail remain below it. They do not form a secure readable word.

Large opening N and small rounded following strokes survive at left; the separated avons run and the long p descenders of supposé remain below the cancellation. The strike covers several connecting strokes, so the reading is moderate confidence.
Rounded O with low n is followed by the low peut run and its rising terminal stroke; the final word retains two distinct downward p loops and a long ser ending under the strike.
The initial i dot, low connected double-m run, detached acute accent, d loop and final tall crossed t remain visible above and below the deletion line.

The word begins with a low open c rather than the tall looped d required by définition. A later upright and low loop survive, but the heavy cancellation merges the intervening and final letters, so the rest of continuité remains uncertain.
One compact angular s sits between the parenthesis strokes: a short upright turns into an oblique curved return. It has no crossbar of the nearby integral-limit t.
The single argument has an oblique rising stroke and low returning hook between the parentheses; the explicit t above the adjacent integral instead has a straight stem and crossbar.

The sole interior glyph rises diagonally from a short low turn and bends into the closing parenthesis; there is no crossing stroke or separately raised glyph. This is the same angular s form seen in the integrals.
Inside the two curved parentheses is one narrow s with an upright entry and diagonal return. No independent t crossbar is present.
A hooked lower turn and diagonal rising stroke form one s between distinct parentheses; the small central thickening is the letter turn, with no horizontal t crossbar.

The opening d has a looped foot and long rising ascender, followed by the separate apostrophe and very compressed low o/u strokes. The brief group occupies the space immediately before the final inequality.

The subscript position contains a dark cluster of diagonal deletion strokes. A downward stem and short upper projection survive, but neither can be separated confidently from the cancellation to establish t.
